channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Indian Photo Festival Open Call 2026
item.description: The Indian Photo Festival invites photographers, visual storytellers, artists, curators, collectives, archives, galleries and organisations worldwide to submit work for the exhibitions of its 12th edition, held in Hyderabad from 26 November 2026 to 3 January 2027. The theme is open: the festival welcomes cohesive bodies of work from all genres of photography and lens-based storytelling, including documentary, conceptual, fine art, portraiture, landscape, street, experimental practices, archival projects and mixed media, and states that submissions are judged on artistic merit, originality, coherence, visual quality, storytelling and conceptual strength rather than genre. Alongside the exhibition call, the festival is also inviting published, self-published, independently produced and dummy photobooks, as well as zines, for the Indian Photo Festival Photobook Exhibition; photobooks are submitted as a single PDF of all pages and spreads, and selected titles are invited to send one physical copy for display. Selected exhibition projects are professionally produced and exhibited by the festival at no cost to the participant, which bears the production costs of exhibition prints and display materials. There is no entry fee. Submissions require a minimum of 15 and a maximum of 30 images, plus an artist statement and biography of up to 500 words each. Only shortlisted applicants are contacted. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Gift of Art 2026 · Hal Bromm Gallery
item.description: Hal Bromm established Tribeca's first contemporary gallery in 1975, showing early minimal and conceptual work by Carl Andre, Rosemarie Castoro, Victor Burgin and John Hilliard, and giving early solo exhibitions to Krzysztof Wodiczko, Keith Haring and David Wojnarowicz. The gallery shows photography as a matter of course: its summer 2026 exhibition photo·graph surveyed contemporary photographic practice with work by Bernd and Hilla Becher, Renate Aller, Slava Mogutin and others. Since the 1980s THE GIFT OF ART has been the gallery's annual holiday tradition, in which artists are invited to make unique, saleable artworks as ornaments to adorn the gallery tree - often with overtly political themes that challenged the usual sugar plums and Christmas angels. Last year's edition featured over 100 handmade ornaments by more than 60 artists from around the globe. For 2026 the gallery is expanding the show to include artist-made prints, so the work can live in a home year-round. Each artist may submit up to three ornaments and two prints, and may enter one or both categories. Submissions are reviewed on a rolling basis and artists are notified no later than 10 October 2026. Both ornaments and prints are for sale at the gallery throughout December, with 30% of proceeds going to Rehabilitation Through the Arts, which has run arts programming in New York prisons since 1996. The exhibition runs 1 to 19 December 2026. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: searching for beauty · A Smith Gallery
item.description: A Smith Gallery in Johnson City, Texas announces "searching for beauty", the next in its long-running series of juried online photography exhibitions. The juror is Wendi Schneider. Selected work is shown in the gallery's online exhibition from 16 October to 26 November 2026, with a reception on 31 October 2026 at 3pm CST and a GalleryTalk video posted in ASG Conversations. A Smith runs these calls on a rolling calendar and typically selects several dozen images for the online gallery and an accompanying exhibition catalogue; its calls are open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide working in all photographic mediums, and work previously exhibited in an A Smith Gallery competition is not eligible. The full prospectus, including the entry fee and image limits, had not yet been published at the time of listing - check the gallery's Calls for Entry page for the entry form once the call opens. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: animalia · A Smith Gallery
item.description: A Smith Gallery in Johnson City, Texas announces "animalia", a juried online photography exhibition on animals, juried by Traer Scott. Selected work is shown in the gallery's online exhibition from 27 November 2026 to 7 January 2027, with a reception on 26 December 2026 at 3pm CST and a GalleryTalk video posted in ASG Conversations. A Smith runs these calls on a rolling calendar and typically selects several dozen images for the online gallery and an accompanying exhibition catalogue; its calls are open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide working in all photographic mediums, and work previously exhibited in an A Smith Gallery competition is not eligible. The full prospectus, including the entry fee and image limits, had not yet been published at the time of listing - check the gallery's Calls for Entry page for the entry form once the call opens. — Deadline: November 2, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Exhibition Open Call · PS122 Gallery
item.description: PS122 Gallery, the not-for-profit alternative exhibition space that has run out of the city-owned 122 Community Center in New York's East Village since 1979, invites proposals for its 2027 season. A three-person jury of arts professionals will select six curator- and/or artist-led exhibitions, each running for a month in the gallery's roughly 1,000 square foot space, with exhibitions scheduled across February, March, April, June, September and October 2027. Proposals must involve at least two artists working in any medium, and either the curator or the artists must live in one of the five New York City boroughs; collectives are encouraged, as are experimental uses of the space, in which case public programmes with an aesthetic component are welcomed but not required. Currently enrolled students are not eligible and each applicant is limited to one submission. The application is free and asks for a 500-word exhibition proposal, the names of the confirmed participating artists, a combined PDF of up to ten images of work, installation shots or a proposed layout with captions, and a combined PDF of CVs for everyone involved. Held annually since the 1986-87 season and restarted in 2023, the open call helped define the gallery's history: it gave early exhibitions to Peter Halley, Keith Haring and Amy Sillman, and the programme has shown Nan Goldin, Barbara Kruger, Louise Bourgeois, Glenn Ligon, Alfredo Jaar, Kiki Smith and David Wojnarowicz among hundreds of others. The gallery is a programme of Painting Space 122 Inc, an artist-run cooperative, and is supported in part by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs. Applicants are notified in October 2026. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Forum Box Open Call 2028
item.description: Forum Box is an artist-run cooperative gallery on the Helsinki waterfront with roughly 300 square metres of exhibition space, and it is now taking proposals for its 2028 programme. Artists, curators and working groups may apply for the whole space or for one or two of its three rooms — Permanto (about 65 m², three continuous walls, 5.6 m ceiling), Monttu (about 70 m², divided by stairs) and Parvi (about 90 m², 4.2 m ceiling and the most wall space). The standard slot is five weeks including installation, and for 2028 shorter project-based exhibitions and performances can also be proposed. Selection is made by an exhibition working group of member artists together with the executive director, and every selected artist is offered a member of Forum Box as a peer contact through the process. Applying is free: a single PDF of no more than 4MB containing the gallery's application form, an exhibition or project plan of up to two A4 pages, CVs and around ten images of recent work, emailed by 1pm Finnish time on 7 September 2026. Exhibiting artists currently pay a space rent — €280 for four weeks in the whole gallery or €100 for one room, dropping to €125 and €70 for a single week — which covers communication, marketing, invigilation and sales handling, and the cooperative states it aims to be entirely rent-free by 2028 and has reduced rents every year since 2020; a 40% commission (plus VAT) applies to work sold. Two conditions are worth reading before applying: solo exhibitions carry a five-year minimum interval between shows at Forum Box, and artists may not hold a solo exhibition elsewhere in the Helsinki metropolitan area in the twelve months before their own. A separate, rent-free strand in the same application window seeks a proposal for the Lux Galleries programme of the Lux Helsinki light art festival, on view 30 December 2027 to 9 January 2028, for which the five-year interval does not apply. All applicants hear by the end of October 2026. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: Free (€70–€280 space rent if selected). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Fool's World Vol. 2.2
item.description: The Fool's World is a small travel literary magazine of poetry, prose and visual art, launched by the team behind Raleigh Review, and its summer reading window closes on 1 September. The visual art category is open to photographers in two forms: up to five individual works submitted as separate files, or a single PDF photo essay or series of up to twelve images, sequenced in the order it should be published and unified in theme or style, with a short statement. The editors read travel broadly — 'a deliciously ambiguous term', in their words — and say the work may be inspired by travel, depict travel itself, or simply reflect movement, as long as the experience is the photographer's own. Only previously unpublished work is considered and AI-generated submissions are banned outright. Submissions are free through the magazine's Duosuma portal, and the team aims to respond within four to six weeks. Physical works should be photographed cleanly, without glare or visible canvas edges unless that is an intentional choice, and accepted work may be asked to be rephotographed to meet print standards. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Fragments of the Everyday · Exposure Photo Gallery
item.description: Exposure Photo Gallery's third open call invites photographers to submit images that find meaning in the world around us — places, people, gestures, scenes and moments, from the extraordinary to the seemingly ordinary. There is no single way to interpret the everyday: it can be found on a street or in a remote landscape, in a face, a piece of architecture, an object, a spontaneous scene or a deliberate composition; what matters is the photographer's perspective. The juror is Steve McCurry, the American photographer whose Afghan Girl is among the most recognisable photographs in the world and who has spent more than five decades portraying cultures, people and scenes of everyday life. Selected work is shown in a group exhibition at the gallery in Río Tercero, Córdoba: a Gold, a Silver and a Bronze Award, ten Honorable Mentions whose prints hang in the physical show, thirty-seven Juror's Selections shown digitally, and special recognitions reserved for photographers from Córdoba Province. The Gold Award winner also takes US$500 and a solo exhibition at the gallery, on a date arranged with the artist. Selected and winning works appear in a print-on-demand exhibition book, and an Online Gallery Special Recognition marks roughly the top 7.5 per cent of entries. All awards are issued as digital diplomas. Fees are tiered by image count and there is no cap on how many photographs may be submitted. Entries close 31 March 2027 at 11:59 PM Pacific time; winners are announced 3 May 2027 and hi-res files are due 14 May. — Deadline: March 31, 2027. Fee: $10–$30. Prize: $500 + solo exhibition (Gold Award).

item.title: Kirloskar Art Grant 2026 · S. L. Kirloskar CSR Foundation
item.description: The second edition of the S. L. Kirloskar CSR Foundation's annual grant for lens-based practitioners, supporting artists whose work interrogates contemporary relationships between people, environments and systems in an age of globalisation, digital saturation and cultural transformation. The Foundation frames photography and moving image not only as tools of representation but as instruments for questioning dominant narratives and creating new ones, and invites proposals engaging critically with sustainability and environment, science and innovation, biodiversity and nature, culture and heritage, or community and social change. Two recipients — one photographer and one moving-image artist — are selected by a jury, each receiving a production grant of INR 5 lakh, of which up to 35 per cent may be taken as an artist fee or honorarium, plus opportunities to show the completed project at Kirloskar Group premises and other venues across India. Applications are open to emerging practitioners working in documentary, conceptual, experimental or new media formats who reside in India and hold Indian citizenship; individuals and artist duos or collectives may apply. Submissions go by email and comprise a project proposal of up to 1,000 words, a 500-word artist statement, a portfolio of five to ten captioned images or videos as a PDF under 5 MB, a CV, a budget breakdown and a project timeline. Equipment purchases are not covered, though project-related consumables such as film, cards, ink and paper are. The project period runs 21 September 2026 to 21 March 2027, and copyright remains with the artist. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: INR 5 lakh cash grant each (2 awards).

item.title: Photographic Nights of Selma 2026
item.description: The seventh edition of a festival founded by French photographer Stéphane Kossmann — who also founded Les Nuits Photographiques de Pierrevert — in partnership with Foot Soldier Park and Arts Revive in Selma, Alabama. Around thirty selected artist projects are shown each evening on a giant outdoor screen, with daytime given over to exhibitions across the Selma area, encounters between photographers and the public, portfolio readings and conferences. There is no set theme: the artistic committee asks only for a unique perspective and a clearly asserted point of view in a series of fifteen to thirty photographs, and is looking for a broad panorama of recent work of all kinds — reflections on society, landscape, fashion, portraiture, still life, explorations of intimacy, or proposals diverging from the current zeitgeist. Selected series are presented as photo-sound montages of no more than four minutes; the festival's video and sound editors can build the montage, or photographers may submit their own edit, and an original soundtrack may be supplied. Each selected photographer commits to attending the evening of their screening and the following day; photographers stay in local homes for the duration, limited to fifteen places, with lunches covered by the festival and travel at the photographer's own expense. Prizes are awarded at the end by a jury of figures from photography and the arts and by the public, and the Jury Prize carries an invitation with travel expenses covered to the Nuits Photographiques de Pierrevert in the south of France in the last week of July 2027. Applicants must declare any use of image-generation tools. The festival runs 6–7 November 2026 and access to exhibitions, screenings and conferences is free. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Santu Mofokeng Foundation Photography Prize 2026
item.description: A new national award from the Santu Mofokeng Foundation, established in honour of one of South Africa's most influential photographers and dedicated to recognising and supporting outstanding emerging photographers working in the country. Through a national open call the Foundation seeks artists whose work shows a thoughtful and compelling engagement with the photographic medium, reflecting the depth, sensitivity and critical awareness that characterised Mofokeng's own practice, and aims to provide recognition, visibility and professional support at a pivotal stage in a career. The inaugural award carries a R100,000 cash prize together with editorial support, an artist profile and opportunities for future exhibition presentation through the programmes of Latitudes, the Foundation's promotional and platform partner. Entry is open to independent practitioners living and working in South Africa; the application form sets an age ceiling of 45 and asks for a cohesive body of ten to fifteen photographs made within the past five years, alongside a portrait image, a recent biography and statements describing the applicant's practice, the submitted body of work and why they would be a strong recipient. The Foundation was established in 2015, when Mofokeng donated his photographic work and copyright to it, and works to preserve, research and share his legacy while supporting contemporary photographic practice through exhibitions, publications and public programmes. Applications close on 15 October 2026. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: R100,000.

item.title: Helpmann Fellowships 2026 · Helpmann Academy
item.description: Three fellowships of up to A$7,500 for emerging South Australian creatives, funded by the James & Diana Ramsay Foundation. The fellowships are self-determined: applicants propose their own bold, ambitious project, which may be the creation of new work, an exhibition, a residency or internship, touring, specialised training, a longer professional development programme, or a combination. Photography is one of nineteen disciplines on the application form, alongside painting, sculpture, moving image, printmaking, new media and curatorial practice. Applicants must be final-year students or graduates within five years of a supported degree at Adelaide University, Flinders University, the University of Adelaide or the University of South Australia, and must currently reside in South Australia; master's and PhD candidates qualify only through their undergraduate or honours study. Applications are assessed on artistic merit, alignment with career development, feasibility, commitment to learning and level of ambition, and require an artist CV, academic transcript, budget on the Academy's template, timeline, project confirmations, two letters of support and four to six images or one to two audio-visual demos. Funded activity must take place between 1 January and 31 December 2027. There is no application fee. Outcomes are notified within four weeks of the closing date and fellowships are presented at a private event in October. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: A$7,500 × 3.

item.title: 8th Annual Art + Stroll
item.description: A juried exhibition of original 2D and 3D fine art in all mediums and styles, staged across downtown Fort Lauderdale by Business for the Arts of Broward. Selected work hangs for a week in the lobbies of 200 and 201 East Las Olas Boulevard — joined this year by Huizenga Park — before the signature Art + Stroll evening on Thursday 12 November 2026, when the Las Olas business district fills with juried visual art, live performances, interactive demonstrations and cultural programming. Selected work is also shown digitally on the BFA Broward website, and each accepted artist receives a complimentary Sip + Stroll VIP ticket. Over $5,000 in cash awards is on offer: $3,000 Best in Show, $1,500 second, $500 third and a $300 Judge's Recognition. The $30 fee covers up to three works; pieces may not exceed 36 inches in their longest dimension or 30 pounds, must arrive exhibition-ready and wired with D-rings, and all work may be offered for sale with BFA retaining 25 per cent commission. Open to artists 18 and over. Note that the CaFE application portal does not open until 17 August 2026. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: $5,300 across four awards.

item.title: Pet Project
item.description: The Bedford's annual juried exhibition returns with Pet Project, a whimsical spin through the joy of the animal companions who captivate us with their larger-than-life personalities and quirks — a playful menagerie of muses and mischief-makers who slither, flutter, scamper and pounce their way into our lives. The call is open to all media and to US-based artists 18 and over; only artwork about pets will be juried. Artists may submit up to three works, with no size limit in principle though the gallery reserves the right to decline exceptionally large or cumbersome pieces, and 2D work must arrive framed where applicable and ready to hang. Jurors are to be announced, and $2,000 in cash prizes will be given as juror awards. The $40 entry fee is waived for anyone who donates $50 or more to the Bedford before applying, using a donor code entered at checkout. Notice of participation goes out 23 April 2027, work is delivered 14–18 June and the exhibition runs 10 July to 12 September 2027 at the Bedford Gallery in the Lesher Center for the Arts, opening with a party on 10 July. Artists are encouraged but not required to list work for sale; the gallery's commission structure is 60 per cent of the sale price to the artist and 40 per cent retained. — Deadline: March 24, 2027. Fee: $40 (free for Bedford donors of $50+). Prize: $2,000 in juror awards.

item.title: Josephine Ulrick and Win Schubert Photography Award 2026 · HOTA, Home of the Arts
item.description: Queensland's richest acquisitive photographic prize returns to HOTA Gallery on the Gold Coast: A$25,000 and acquisition into the HOTA Collection for the winner, plus a A$5,000 People's Choice Award decided by public vote. Submissions are invited across the traditional and expanded medium, including photocollage, sculpture, projection, installation and cameraless photography. Finalists are chosen by a panel of 2018 award winner Tamara Dean, UNSW Galleries director José Da Silva and independent writer and curator Mikala Tai, and are shown in the award exhibition at HOTA Gallery from 28 November 2026 to 7 March 2027. Previous winners include Polly Borland, Merilyn Fairskye, Shaun Gladwell, Polixeni Papapetrou, Darren Sylvester and Justine Varga. Entrants must be 18 or over and Australian citizens or permanent residents; individuals and groups may enter, but nobody may appear in more than one submission. Entry is limited to one artwork, created on or after 11 May 2025 and no larger than 300 cm in any dimension including frame or mount, and work must be available for the full exhibition period. AI may be used provided the extent of that use is clearly described in the submission. The entry fee has been reduced to A$15, with A$10 Mob Tix for First Nations applicants. Finalists are notified by email or phone and have seven days to accept; the winner is announced at the exhibition opening. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: A$15 (A$10 Mob Tix). Prize: A$25,000 acquisitive + A$5,000 People's Choice.

item.title: MYPH Photography Prize 2026 · MYPH
item.description: The third annual, free prize from the MYPH school of conceptual and art photography, open to Ukrainian citizens living in Ukraine or abroad who have no more than five years of active practice with the photographic medium — which MYPH defines as conscious, regular, consistent work in art photography, from making one's own projects and series to exhibitions, competitions, residencies, portfolio reviews, publication and engagement with the artistic community. Fine art, conceptual and documentary photography are all invited, and every photographic technique and form of visual manipulation is accepted, from analogue shooting to digital collage and experiment. Applicants submit a series or project of eight to ten photographs made in 2025 or 2026; ongoing projects are welcome, and last year's winners may enter with new work. The Grand Prix takes a Fujifilm X-series camera and lens, a 50,000 UAH MYPH tuition certificate, membership of the Ukrainian Association of Professional Photographers, and showings at Art Market Budapest and Art Kyiv Fair; second and third places take MYPH tuition certificates of 25,000 and 10,000 UAH rather than prize money, and a separate Fujifilm 'Best Debut' prize goes to an author showing a series publicly for the first time. Eight finalists exhibit together at Dymchuk Gallery in Kyiv, with the show travelling in Ukraine and abroad as part of MYPH Photo Festival, and partner prizes include a 15,000 UAH cash award for one woman photographer, print production, photobooks and further tuition certificates. Applicants must be 18 at the time of applying. Finalists are announced on 13 October 2026 and the winners at the exhibition ceremony on 23 October. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Fujifilm camera + 50,000 UAH tuition.

item.title: Exposure 2027 International Open Call
item.description: The Exposure Photography Festival is a month-long celebration of photography that takes over Alberta every February. Its International Open Call is for photographers and visual artists anywhere in the world, at any stage of their career, who incorporate, celebrate or challenge the photographic medium. There is no set theme and no preferred style: images can be shot in any format with any camera and may include collage or experimental approaches. Jurors are given an open mandate and weigh artistic strength, contemporary relevance and resonance, how the work would read in a public exhibition, and curatorial breadth across practices, subject matter, geographic and cultural contexts and career stages. Selected artists show in a group exhibition at TRUCK Contemporary Art in Mohkinstis (Calgary) for the whole of February 2027, free and open to the public, and receive a CA$456 artist fee calculated according to CARFAC guidelines, a CA$50 production expense allocation and a 20 per cent discount with print partner ABL Imaging to prepare the work; mounting and framing decisions are made collaboratively with Exposure's curatorial team. Selected images from every exhibiting artist also appear in a public billboard exhibition on Pattison Outdoor digital screens around Calgary, and each artist gets a profile on Exposure's website alongside social and press promotion. Submit at least five images from a strong, connected series with a short statement; the fee covers up to five images, with further images CA$5 each up to ten in total. Ten fee waivers are available to artists facing economic hardship, decided first come first served with a reply inside 48 hours, and photographers based in non-high-income countries can apply free through a separate form. The 2027 jury will be one international juror, one Exposure board member and the festival manager, to be announced. Notification October 31, 2026; prints due December 2026. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: CA$45 (+CA$5 per extra image). Prize: CA$456 artist fee + Exhibition.

item.title: Exposure 2027 North West Showcase
item.description: The North West Showcase is the Exposure Photography Festival's spotlight on emerging photographic talent in western and northern Canada, running alongside its international call each February. It is open to emerging artists resident in Alberta, British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Yukon and the Northwest Territories; Exposure defines an emerging artist as someone in the early stages of publicly presenting or publishing their work, a definition that deliberately does not rest on age, formal education or traditional career milestones. There is no theme. Work can be shot in any format with any camera and may include collage or experimental approaches, and jurors weigh artistic strength, contemporary relevance, exhibition potential and the curatorial breadth of the selection as a whole. Selected artists show in a group exhibition at TRUCK Contemporary Art in Calgary for the whole of February 2027, free to the public, and receive a CA$456 artist fee set by CARFAC guidelines, a CA$50 production expense allocation and a 40 per cent discount with print partner ABL Imaging. Selected images also go up in a public billboard exhibition on Pattison Outdoor digital screens across Calgary, with an artist profile on Exposure's site plus social and press promotion. Showcase artists are additionally eligible for Exposure's Emerging Photographer of the Year Award, which gives its recipient a solo show at the following year's festival. Submit at least eight images from a connected series with a short statement; the fee covers up to ten images, with further images CA$5 each to a maximum of fifteen. Ten hardship fee waivers are available first come first served, and Alberta's Immigrant Council for Arts Innovation submits five free applications for its members each year. The jury will be one national juror, two representatives of Calgary's photography community, an Exposure board member and the festival manager, to be announced. Notification October 31, 2026. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: CA$35 (+CA$5 per extra image). Prize: CA$456 artist fee + Exhibition.

item.title: Convergence of Creativity 2026 — Unexpected: Look Again! · City of San Ramon
item.description: The City of San Ramon's third annual juried exhibition takes 'Unexpected — Look Again!' as its theme, asking artists to find the surprising, unconventional, humorous, mysterious or unforeseen in everyday objects, nature, relationships, memories, materials or imagination, whether read literally or conceptually. Photography is one of six named categories, alongside mixed media and printmaking, painting, drawing, ceramics, sculpture and textiles, and digital art; both two- and three-dimensional work is accepted. It is an annual event featuring work from artists around the country, open to anyone aged 16 through senior adults. Work must be original and conceived and created entirely by the entering artist, with no AI-generated work accepted, and pieces shown in last year's San Ramon juried exhibits are not eligible. Two-dimensional work may not exceed 30 by 40 inches including the frame and 40 pounds; three-dimensional work must stay within 18 inches each way and 50 pounds. Accepted work is hung on a Walker display system and must arrive exhibit-ready, cleanly framed and wired with D-ring hangers. Up to three entries per artist at $15 each, with a $5 student rate via a coupon code. Selection and awards are decided by a blind jury that does not see personal information, and the awards are gift certificates: $150 for Best in Show overall, then $100, $75 and $50 blue, red and white ribbons in each category. The exhibition runs November 14 to December 16 at the Lindsay Dirkx Brown Gallery in the San Ramon Community Center, with a public artists' reception on November 14; sales carry a 20 per cent commission to the city and work must be hand delivered and collected on set dates. Note that the CaFÉ application portal does not open until August 14, 2026, at cityofsanramon.info/unexpected; artists are notified October 16. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: $15 per entry ($5 for students). Prize: Gift certificates up to $150.

item.title: Portraits · MVA Gallery
item.description: National call for portraiture at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, filling both exhibition rooms. Artists, photographers and sculptors at every level are invited: traditional or non-traditional imagery of a single individual, a couple or a group, from a close-up of a face to a half-length or full-body pose, made to read as idealised, neutral, psychological, satirical, celebratory or cultural. The gallery specifically asks for environmental portraits that place a person in the surroundings that explain them, for distorted and surreal approaches, and for self-portraits — formal, informal or the ubiquitous selfie — as a way into questions of identity and perception. All photographic processes are welcome and there is no cutoff date for when the work was made. Open to US residents aged 18 and over; submit 3 to 9 works. Awards are an Art of Distinction award carrying a featured exhibit in the gallery's second room, an optional $200 Director's Choice, honourable mentions that come with free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from every artist shown at the gallery during the year. Framed or gallery-wrapped work up to 48 inches and 45 lbs, wired for hanging; photographs framed in black or white with white or off-white mats if presented traditionally, and plexiglass preferred over glass for shipped pieces. The gallery takes 30% commission and artists cover shipping both ways. Exhibition runs 24 January – 21 February 2027. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Tribute to Small Art 2026 · MVA Gallery
item.description: National call for small-format work at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. Against an age of supersized images, the gallery makes the case for smallness: work no longer than 18 inches on the longest side, with no restriction on style or subject matter. Artists, photographers and sculptors at every level are invited and all photographic processes are welcome; there is no cutoff date for when the work was made. Open to US residents aged 18 and over; submit 3 to 9 works. Awards are an Art of Distinction award carrying a featured exhibit in the gallery's second room, an optional $200 Director's Choice, honourable mentions that come with free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from every artist shown at the gallery during the year. Work must be wired for hanging; photographs framed in black or white with white or off-white mats if presented traditionally, and plexiglass preferred over glass for shipped pieces. The gallery takes 30% commission and artists cover shipping both ways. Exhibition runs 24 January – 21 February 2027. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Group Show #19
item.description: Open call for seven solo wall presentations in Group Show #19 at New & Abstract's gallery in central Berlin, staged during Berlin Art Week. The gallery asks for new and innovative positions across all media — painting, drawing and printmaking through sculpture, installation and wall-mounted objects, and explicitly photography, digital works and mixed media — and says only: surprise us with your style. Seven winners are chosen to show physically, each given three to four metres of wall on which one or more works are hung in consultation with the gallery; a further twenty honourable mentions are featured on the gallery's Instagram feed and stories. Work must be no larger than 200 × 200 cm, available for the exhibition and offered for sale both on site and in the online gallery, with the artist keeping 60% of any sale. Exhibited works are insured for the run; work must reach Berlin at the artist's own arrangement, and the artist covers return shipping if a piece comes back. Founded in 2019 as an Instagram platform, New & Abstract has shown more than a hundred artists on 100 square metres in Berlin since June 2024. Entry is a €20 processing fee per artwork submitted, non-refundable, and the gallery states plainly that no further costs arise if you are selected for the exhibition, the online gallery or Instagram promotion. Open worldwide to artists aged 18 and over. Winners and honourable mentions are announced by 24 August; work must reach Berlin by 7 September; the show runs 10–24 September 2026 with an opening reception on 10 September. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: €20 per artwork. Prize: Exhibition during Berlin Art Week.

item.title: Artist Project Support Grant 2027
item.description: The Auburn Arts Commission redistributes part of its 4Culture Arts Sustained Support funding as small project grants for artists, typically $500 to $1,000, awarded competitively. The programme funds arts projects and programmes that take place inside the city limits of Auburn, Washington during the 2027 calendar year and that are free and open to the general public for at least part of their run — a photographic exhibition, a documentary screening, a workshop series or a community photo project all qualify, so long as access is not restricted to members or invitees. Strong applications are expected to show real community impact alongside innovation and excellence in the field. Open to artists residing in the Pacific Northwest (Washington, Oregon and Idaho). Scholarships and tuition support, ticket subsidies, projects supporting religious activities or political organisations, and projects that primarily serve an organisation's own membership are not eligible; City of Auburn staff and Arts Commission members may not apply. There is no application fee. Applications are read by a peer panel of arts professionals familiar with Auburn, the granting committee meets in October 2026, and applicants hear results in mid-November. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $500–$1,000.

item.title: 2027 CVG Show · Collective Visions Gallery
item.description: Twentieth annual all-media juried competition at Collective Visions Gallery in Bremerton, Washington, with Photography/Digital as one of three judged categories alongside Two-Dimensional and Three-Dimensional art. There is no theme — artists are asked simply for their strongest work in any medium or genre. Up to $10,000 in cash and purchase prizes is awarded across the categories. The juror is Jessica Wilks, Director of Curatorial and Interpretation at the Tacoma Art Museum, where she oversees exhibitions, collections and interpretive strategy after more than twenty years of museum work; her current projects include a reinstallation of the museum's permanent collection and a focused exhibition of Cree artist Kent Monkman. Jurying is blind — entrants' names and cities are withheld from the juror — and awards are judged in person from the original works rather than from files. Open to Washington State and Oregon residents aged 18 or over as of August 18, 2026. Work must have been completed on or after January 1, 2022, and pieces made in a class or workshop or under an instructor's direction are not eligible. Entrants must submit two works; a single entry is not accepted, and a third and fourth may be added at $10 each. AI-generated imagery is not accepted, though standard digital editing — sharpening, noise reduction, colour correction — is allowed for photo and digital work. Work sold during the show carries a 40% gallery commission. Submissions open August 18, 2026 and close November 7. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: $45 (2 works) + $10 each additional. Prize: Up to $10,000 in cash and purchase prizes.

item.title: Wonder · Arts Alpharetta
item.description: Juried winter exhibition at the Alpharetta Arts Center, presented by Arts Alpharetta in partnership with the City of Alpharetta Cultural Services. Wonder invites work that captures seasonal awe and enchantment — shimmering light, quiet reflection, the joy of discovery, and the extraordinary hidden within the everyday. Photography is among the accepted media, alongside drawing, painting, mixed media, printmaking, sculpture, kinetic art, ceramics, fiber and folk art. Artists may submit up to three works, one artwork per entry. All work must be original in concept, composition and execution; reproductions of original works are not eligible, and pieces previously shown in the Arts Center's main gallery cannot be re-entered. Accepted work must arrive gallery-ready and wired to hang, and may be delivered in person or shipped with a prepaid return label. The exhibition runs November 24, 2026 to January 9, 2027, with a reception on Friday, December 4. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: $15 per entry. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2028 Solo Exhibit Series · Pennswood Art Gallery
item.description: Open call for solo exhibitions at Pennswood Art Gallery in Newtown, Pennsylvania, which has shown the work of nationally and regionally prominent artists and artisans for more than forty years. Six exhibits are mounted each year, each showcasing a different style, medium, technique or approach, and photography is named among the accepted media — recent solo shows have included black-and-white photographic work. Applications are free: artists submit five to eight images representative of the style or medium of the proposed exhibit, and proposals are scored on creativity, execution and saleability. Selected artists agree to a 20% gallery commission, must make at least 80% of exhibited work available for sale, and present an in-person artist talk at the opening. Artists with a prior connection to Pennswood Village and its surroundings are awarded additional points. Jury decisions are made by December 1, 2026 for exhibits running through 2028. Residents of Pennswood Village are not eligible. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: 101 Art Book: Face Edition · Arts to Hearts Project
item.description: Fourteenth edition of the 101 Art Book series, a curated hardcover publication that gathers 101 contemporary artists around a single theme. Face invites work that reads the human face in every register — portraiture and self-portraiture, faces glimpsed in clouds, architecture or machines, faces as icons, and the face as data in an age of facial recognition, surveillance and deepfakes. Realistic, abstract, conceptual, symbolic, surreal and experimental approaches are all eligible, and photography is explicitly named among the accepted disciplines. One artist receives the Face Edition Award: a USD 500 cash prize, a four-page editorial feature in Arts to Hearts Magazine, a custom glass trophy and a Certificate of Excellence; two further artists receive Jury Recognition Awards with the same feature, trophy and certificate. Previously exhibited, published or sold work is accepted so long as the artist holds the rights, and artists retain full copyright throughout. Open internationally to emerging, mid-career and established artists 18 and over; results are announced within three weeks of the deadline. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: $21–$100 (tiered, 1–20 images). Prize: $500 + 4-page magazine feature.

item.title: The Fifty: 50 Billboards 50 States · VSCO
item.description: Nationwide open call selecting fifty US-based photographers — one from every state — to have their work printed on billboards across the country, licensed and paid for by VSCO. No entry fee. Open to photographers aged 18 and over residing in the United States. Entries are made by posting work to a VSCO account tagged #TheFifty plus the hashtag for the photographer's state (e.g. #OHIO), with a short caption about the image or series and the state added to the profile bio; 3–5 images from a cohesive series are recommended. VSCO's curation team reviews every submission and notifies selected photographers on a rolling basis, with announcements published on the VSCO journal. Selected work may also be carried into editorial features, curation and further licensing opportunities. Billboard formats vary by state, and selected work may instead be shown through alternative large-format displays, posters or public installations. Photographs including recognisable people require a model release, and selected photographers must supply a high-resolution file suitable for large-format printing. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Billboard exhibition + paid licensing.

item.title: Photographer in Residence 2027 · Worthless Studios
item.description: One-month analog photography residency inside a 1973 Airstream trailer converted into a fully equipped black-and-white darkroom, parked at partner sites across the five boroughs of New York City. Seven artists are selected for 2027, one per month from April to October, each receiving 24/7 access to the Airstream darkroom for four weeks, a $1,500 artist stipend, free film, paper and chemistry, two free workshops on scanning and digital printing with Brooklyn PrintWorks, press packet materials and the option to host a public program. Host partners include Alice Austen House, Inspiration Point, The Green-Wood Cemetery, The Center for Arts and Advocacy, The Lower Eastside Girls Club and NYC Parks; residents may also propose their own site. Applicants need prior independent darkroom experience, must commit a minimum of 20 hours a week in the Airstream, and cannot be enrolled in — or about to enter — an art-related degree program. Applications are free and made through SlideRoom. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,500 stipend + darkroom, film and materials.

item.title: Photo Fringe 2026 — Feedback Loop
item.description: Photo Fringe is a volunteer-led registered charity that has run an open-platform photography festival on a DIY, collectively-funded model since 2003. Registration is now open for the 2026 edition, which runs 2–31 October across Brighton & Hove, Portsmouth and Newhaven with launch events on Friday 2 October. Anyone can take part: artists, photographers, collectives, curators and organisations register their own self-curated exhibition and are then listed in the official festival programme and on photofringe.org, given marketing resources and exhibitor guidance, and folded into a city-wide trail that helps audiences find the work. Exhibitors are responsible for finding and managing their own venue, though the festival shares venue leads and connects artists looking for larger shared spaces; online-only exhibitions are equally welcome, and Photo Fringe events such as artist talks, workshops and photo walks are listed free. The 2026 theme is Feedback Loop — a cycle of action and response, thinking about how images circulate and change as they are seen, shared, interpreted and reworked, and what becomes possible when work is made with others rather than alone. Responding to the theme is encouraged but not compulsory. Contributions towards the festival are £125 for a solo exhibition at a venue and online, £150 for a group exhibition, £60 for solo online-only and £100 for group online-only, all subsidised; a small number of bursaries are available for exhibitors who cannot afford a contribution, by emailing the festival. All registered exhibitors are automatically entered for the Danny Wilson Memorial Awards, supported by Photoworks, whose prizes include a bursary, mentoring sessions and artist talks. Registration closes 1 September 2026. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: £125 solo / £150 group (online-only £60 / £100); bursaries available. Prize: Exhibition + Bursary.

item.title: Shrode Photography Competition and Exhibit 2026 · Cedarhurst Center for the Arts
item.description: Cedarhurst Center for the Arts is an AAM-accredited museum and sculpture park in Mount Vernon, Illinois, and its annual Shrode Photography Competition is a juried competition and exhibition for photographic film and digital photographs. Cedarhurst invites an established photography professional to judge; after viewing each digital entry individually the judge selects the works accepted into the exhibition and the top awards. Work must be the entrant's original work made within the past three years (2023 or later) and not previously shown in a Cedarhurst or Shrode Art Center competition or exhibition. Submissions may carry an inconspicuous watermark for judging, but accepted photographs must be printed watermark-free and a clean digital file supplied for marketing use. Each artist may submit up to two entry forms at $25 each ($20 for Cedarhurst members), three photographs per form, for a maximum of six photographs judged. All submissions are digital — JPEG or TIFF, each file named with the artist's last name and entry number — and must be received by 5pm on Wednesday 26 August 2026; images on a non-returnable USB flash drive are also accepted. Accepted artists are emailed by the end of the day on 2 September 2026, and accepted work, framed and wired for hanging, must arrive at Shrode Art Center by 25 September. The exhibition runs 4 October 2026 – 10 January 2027 with an awards reception on Saturday 3 October, and closes with an Art Chat hosted by Shrode Art Center director Carrie Stover on 10 January. Awards are Best of Show $500, 1st Place $250, 2nd Place $200 and a People's Choice Award of $100 announced at the close of the show, with honorable mention certificates at the judge's discretion. Entry is open to artists 18 and older living south of Interstate 70, including the Charleston, Illinois area. — Deadline: August 26, 2026. Fee: $25 for up to 3 photos ($20 members). Prize: $500 / $250 / $200 + Exhibition.

item.title: Out of Shape · 3017 Gallery
item.description: Out of Shape celebrates unconventional forms, irregular edges and artwork that moves beyond the traditional rectangle. The gallery is looking for work that treats shape as both a compositional element and a physical object — shaped supports, abstracted forms, irregular compositions, unconventional framing, sculptural wall pieces and other inventive approaches to form, whether organic or geometric, subtle or dramatic. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, fiber, woodworking, mixed media and printmaking, provided the work engages with the theme through form, structure or presentation. 3017 Gallery is a small contemporary gallery in the lower level of ArtisanABQ in Albuquerque, New Mexico, running a monthly themed open call with an opening on the second Saturday of every month. Entry is free; sales are processed through the gallery on a 30% commission. Between three and seven works are required for consideration, delivered ready to hang — two-dimensional work such as framed photographs properly wired, works on paper framed. Applicants send an artist bio of up to 150 words in the third person along with the title, medium, dimensions and price of each piece, and selected artists are notified shortly after submissions close. The exhibition opens on 12 September 2026. — Deadline: August 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Uncanny · 3017 Gallery
item.description: Uncanny explores the eerie, the mysterious and the unexplainable, and welcomes artwork that embraces the strange, surreal and unsettling — haunting figures, dreamlike landscapes, cryptic symbolism, eerie atmospheres and imagined creatures. Whether psychological, supernatural, grotesque or quietly unsettling, the gallery is after work that evokes curiosity, tension and wonder and invites viewers into worlds that defy explanation. Photography and digital media are named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, fiber, woodworking, mixed media and printmaking. 3017 Gallery is a small contemporary gallery in the lower level of ArtisanABQ in Albuquerque, New Mexico, running a monthly themed open call with an opening on the second Saturday of every month. Entry is free; sales are processed through the gallery on a 30% commission. Between three and seven works are required for consideration, delivered ready to hang — two-dimensional work such as framed photographs properly wired, works on paper framed. Applicants send an artist bio of up to 150 words in the third person along with the title, medium, dimensions and price of each piece, and selected artists are notified shortly after submissions close. The exhibition opens on 10 October 2026. — Deadline: September 26, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Less Is More · 3017 Gallery
item.description: Less Is More is a small-works exhibition open to pieces 12 x 12 inches or smaller, built around the idea that size does not limit presence, meaning or visual impact. The gallery is interested in the experience of engaging with work on an intimate scale, where every piece has the chance to command attention and invite closer observation. Photography and digital media are named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, fiber, woodworking, mixed media and printmaking. 3017 Gallery is a small contemporary gallery in the lower level of ArtisanABQ in Albuquerque, New Mexico, running a monthly themed open call with an opening on the second Saturday of every month. Entry is free; sales are processed through the gallery on a 30% commission. Between three and seven works are required for consideration, delivered ready to hang — two-dimensional work such as framed photographs properly wired, works on paper framed. Applicants send an artist bio of up to 150 words in the third person along with the title, medium, dimensions and price of each piece, and selected artists are notified shortly after submissions close. The exhibition opens on 14 November 2026. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Semioculus XXIII
item.description: Semioculus is an independent international art zine and artist community originally founded in Tartu, Estonia, grown from a hobby project started by a group of college course mates into an international community and published quarterly in digital and limited print runs, dedicated to dark and surreal work from around the world — its own aesthetic keywords are dark, dreamlike, macabre, obscure and surreal. Submissions are open for the twenty-third issue, and the guidelines set no theme beyond that aesthetic: artists are free to send new pieces or older work, provided the publication rights still belong to them. Self-published work and images previously posted to an artist's own website or social media are fine. Any medium that can be published both digitally and in print is accepted as long as it fits the aesthetic; AI-generated work and fan art of any kind are not accepted. Visual art should be sent as JPG, PDF, TIFF or PNG at the highest resolution possible and no lower than 200 DPI, no more than six pieces at a time, with filenames formatted ArtistName_TitleOfWork; poems and flash fiction are also accepted, up to six A5 pages. Submissions are taken by email only, with the artist's name, titles, an optional short text tied to the work and a link to a website or social media in the body of the message. The zine is run as a passion project and cannot currently offer artists payment — it is free to enter, the original artist retains all rights to their work, and selected artists are contacted within one to two weeks of the deadline. Only artists aged 18 and up are accepted, as the zine occasionally features mature themes. Submissions close 16 August 2026. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: GO GREEN · Art Fluent
item.description: Art Fluent's online juried exhibit on the colour green — which sits at the psychological midpoint of the spectrum and is processed by the eye with the least strain of any hue, tied to safety, stability and growth but just as able to tip into envy or unease. The organisers call that range one of the more emotionally loaded colours an artist can work with, and want your version of it. Open worldwide to amateur and professional artists in all fine art media, photography named explicitly among them; work previously selected for an Art Fluent exhibit is not eligible and AI will not be accepted. Curated and juried by Creative Director Amy Matteson Neill with an anonymous committee — there is no personal feedback from jurors. Best of Show takes $750 and two Director's Choice awards take $250 each; all accepted pieces are shown in the online gallery at art-fluent.com. JPEGs are due by midnight MST on November 20, 2026, with notification and the gallery opening by December 18. Entry is $25 for the first piece and $10 for each additional, up to twenty. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $25 + $10 each additional. Prize: $1,250.

item.title: 2026 National Juried Show · Washington Art Association
item.description: The Washington Art Association & Gallery's national juried show, open to artists across the United States and juried by the New York painter Barbara Grossman, who studied at Cooper Union and the Akademie der Künste in Munich and has taught at the Yale School of Art, the New York Studio School and Chautauqua. Original photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, works on paper (drawing, watercolour, printmaking, collage) and sculpture; giclées and other reproductions are not accepted. Work must have been made in the last three years, must not have shown at the gallery before, may not exceed 40 inches in any direction including frame or base, and must be for sale for the run of the show, on which the gallery takes its standard 40% commission. Artists are responsible for shipping both ways and must include a prepaid return label. Up to six entries per artist at $40 for the first three and $5 for each additional. Notification August 24, work delivered September 8–12, and the exhibition runs September 19 – October 17, 2026, opening with a reception on September 19 at the gallery in Washington Depot, Connecticut. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: $40 for up to 3 entries ($5 each additional). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Dezi Art Prize 2026
item.description: Two $1,000 unrestricted cash grants for early-career visual artists, run by Dezi, a career-support platform for artists launching in 2026. Photography is named in the eligible-media list alongside painting, drawing and illustration, sculpture, filmmaking, design, UI/UX design, 2D/3D animation, fashion, and fiber and material arts. Open worldwide to artists 18 and over, one entry per artist per cycle, with no degree, gallery representation or exhibition history required. An independent jury of working arts professionals reviews every submission and scores it on four equally weighted criteria — quality of the work, originality and point of view, the artist statement, and the pitch for the grant — with jurors recusing themselves from any application where they know the applicant. Only the two winners receive cash; the top 30 ranked applicants are featured in Dezine, the platform's magazine, and get a named profile on the Dezi site, the top 20 of those also receive a free one-on-one career audit, and every applicant regardless of ranking is offered a post-close career-guidance interview. Winners agree to credit the prize on any new work made with the funds and to share the finished work within a year for possible inclusion in a future Dezi exhibition. Applications opened on 15 July, the jury reviews through September and winners are announced on 10 October 2026. The application fee is $30 flat with no added processing fees; the $20 early bird closed on 1 August 2026. The organisers offer a discount for students and will consider a waiver on request for anyone else for whom the fee is a barrier. Organised by Phistream LLC and led by founder Nitya Mehrotra, a RISD and SAIC graduate whose work spans animation, public art and gallery exhibition. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: $1,000 x2.

item.title: International Artist Residency — Winter/Spring 2027 · bEam arts
item.description: One- or two-month studio residency in Thessaloniki, Greece, taking up to five artists from different disciplines per period. Applications for the winter/spring 2027 cycle close 24 August 2026 and decisions are confirmed by 4 September; the 2027 periods run monthly from January to July, and artists staying longer than a month can remain in the studios between periods. Each resident gets an individual studio in a shared space with their own key, continuous one-to-one mentorship and assistance, a well-equipped communal workshop, critiques, visits to museums, galleries and artist studios in Thessaloniki, the chance to propose site-specific projects, presentations or workshops, and a group exhibition at the end of each residency where work may be sold. Accommodation is optional. bEam arts is an independent, self-funded organisation that receives no external financial support, so the cost sits with the artist: €1,850 per month with accommodation or €1,000 per month without, duo artists €250 or €150 extra. There is no application fee; selected artists pay a deposit of 50% of the residence fee, refundable if cancelled 30 or more days before the start date. The organisers encourage applicants to seek funding from national arts councils, foundations or universities and will supply letters of invitation and acceptance and tailored wording for funding applications. Open to artists working in any medium; the application asks for an artist statement and a project proposal of up to 250 words each, plus a CV and 5 to 10 portfolio images with dimensions, technique, title and date. — Deadline: August 24, 2026. Fee: Free (€1,000–€1,850/month if selected). Prize: Residency.

item.title: Printed Matter Publisher Work Grant 2026
item.description: Printed Matter's annual programme of unrestricted grants for artists' book publishers, now in its third year and supported by the Wagner Foundation. In 2026 three grants of $10,000 each go to independent presses with a publishing history of one or more years, alongside a featured exhibitor presence at a forthcoming Printed Matter NY or LA Art Book Fair, with the table provided free of charge. The award is unrestricted: funds can cover production and development costs, artists' fees, equipment, studio rent or hired assistance, with no obligation to deliver a specific project. Eligible imprints should be small in scale and published with an independent spirit, without major ongoing distribution support; commercially run studios that only publish client work, and imprints attached to well-resourced institutions, are generally not eligible. The jury is broadly interested in presses that treat the book as a site for experimental artwork, that engage social and political themes with nuance, that give voice to marginalised perspectives, and that back emerging and underrepresented artists regardless of sales prospects. The grant is not aimed at artists seeking to fund a book of their own work, though artists who actively publish others are welcome. Open to publishers based anywhere; international applications encouraged. Past Publisher Work Grant winners cannot apply a second time. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 3 × $10,000 + Art Book Fair table.

item.title: 1st Digital Art Exhibition · Philadelphia Sketch Club
item.description: The Philadelphia Sketch Club — founded in 1860 and the oldest artists' club in the United States — opens its first ever Digital Art Show, an open juried exhibition at its Camac Street galleries. Every submitted work must include a substantial amount of digitally created content, which suits composited, layered and heavily manipulated photo-based work; the club runs a separate annual PHOTOgraphy exhibition for straight photography and does not publish where the line between the two falls. Work must be original, not previously shown at the PSC, framed and wired for hanging, no larger than 24 inches in any dimension excluding the frame and no heavier than 30 lbs; prints deemed low-quality on delivery will not be hung. Artists may submit up to ten works, with a maximum of two accepted per artist. Works made with generative AI are not eligible in any PSC exhibition. Juror Perry Santulli selects the show, and prizes of $300, $200 and $100 are awarded with Contemporary Sketch Club Medals and certificates, plus at least three honourable mentions, presented at the reception on 11 October. All work must be for sale; the club takes 25% commission. The exhibition runs 4–25 October 2026. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: $25 + $10 per piece (members $10 + $10 per piece). Prize: $300 + Sketch Club Medal.

item.title: The Artist's Vision · MVA Gallery
item.description: National open call with no theme at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, filling both exhibition rooms. Artists, photographers and sculptors at every level are asked simply for their finest work — any theme, style or subject matter, traditional, experimental or a synthesis of the two — and the prospectus states plainly that all photographic processes are welcome. Open to US residents aged 18 and over; submit 3 to 9 works, with no cutoff date on when the work was made. The CaFE entry window runs 10 to 31 August 2026. Awards include an Art of Distinction award carrying a featured exhibit in the gallery's second room, an optional $200 Director's Choice, honourable mentions that come with free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from every artist shown at the gallery during the year. Framed or gallery-wrapped work up to 48 inches, wired for hanging; plexiglass preferred over glass for shipped pieces. The gallery takes 30% commission and artists cover shipping both ways. Exhibition runs 24 January – 21 February 2027. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: 40 Over 40 · South x Southeast Photo Gallery
item.description: South x Southeast Gallery invites photographers over the age of 40 to enter its 40 Over 40 open call, curated by Elizabeth Avedon. The call is open to photographers of all backgrounds and experience levels, and all subject matter is welcome — street photography, portraits, nudes, landscapes, nature, wildlife, urban, architecture and documentary work. Selected photographs are shown in the gallery's online exhibition through September and October 2026, with a Zoom reception for the exhibiting photographers on a date to be announced. Entry is by email: images should be JPEG only, 72dpi and 1000 pixels on the longest side, named lastname-firstname-title (for example mccrarynancybigredhouse), zipped into a single file and attached to an email with the subject line '40 Over 40'. The entry fee is $40 for the first four images and $10 for each additional image, paid separately through the gallery's shop. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: $40 for 4 images; $10 each additional. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: On Rose · Looking Glass Photographic Outfitters
item.description: Looking Glass, the independent photographic outfitters in Berkeley, launches On Rose to mark its move to a new home on Rose Street. Photographers are invited to interpret 'rose' as broadly as they like — as a flower, a colour, a symbol, a place, a story, an act of resistance or a moment of renewal. A rose does not need to appear in the picture, but the connection should be visible and meaningful. Each photograph is assigned to one of six categories: The Botanical Rose; Symbol, Story and Metaphor; Rose as Colour; Celebration, Honor and Community; On Rose Street; and They Rose Up. Entry uses a sliding-scale contribution of $5, $10, $15, $20, $25, $30, $40 or $50 — the amount chosen has no effect on judging, selection or awards — and one entry covers up to three photographs. Work is judged anonymously by Bay Area photographers Becky Jaffe, Sarah Deragon and Brandon Ruffin on interpretation of the theme (40%), visual voice and emotional resonance (40%) and photographic execution (20%). The overall winner, category winners and honourable mentions are exhibited at Abrams Claghorn Gallery & Shop in Albany, California in October 2026, with an opening reception; the overall winner also receives a commemorative trophy. Selected photographers are expected to be notified in October 2026. Photographs may be made on film, digital cameras or phones, and older work is welcome, but every entry must begin as a real-world capture by the entrant. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $5–$50 sliding scale. Prize: Exhibition at Abrams Claghorn Gallery + trophy.

item.title: (Not) Food Porn — From Feed to Culture · Der Greif
item.description: Open call from Der Greif, the Munich non-profit for contemporary photography, timed to the International Day of Awareness of Food Loss and Waste on 29 September. The brief asks lens-based artists to work critically at the intersection of food imagery, consumption and culture: highly stylised "food porn" has reshaped how we perceive, desire and celebrate what we eat, and opposing feeds lean into raw, unedited aesthetics, while behind both sits massive global food waste and a rapidly shifting relationship to sustenance. Submissions are one project of up to 10 images, cohesive and not previously featured by Der Greif. Selected work is presented in an online exhibition in Der Greif's Pulse section, and selected artists are invited into a small-group online roundtable critique facilitated by Der Greif staff as part of its Face-to-Face programme, with visibility across Der Greif's international community and a possible invitation to submit a portfolio to Der Greif Studio for sales and commissions. Selection is judged on artistic quality, conceptual clarity, openness to dialogue and process, and engagement with themes of identity and community. Der Greif describes this as a free submission with an optional €5 or €10 donation, but the Picter entry page carries a flat €10 fee; artists who cannot contribute financially can email the organiser for a 50% or 100% discount code. Open to photographers and videographers internationally, particularly emerging and mid-career artists, with no age or regional restriction. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: €10 (waivers available). Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: 34th Tewksbury Juried Art Show · Tewksbury Historical Society
item.description: The Tewksbury Historical Society's juried art show returns for a 34th edition at the Zion Lutheran Christian Education Building in Oldwick, New Jersey, from 3 to 10 October 2026. Any two-dimensional media may be entered, photography explicitly included, with only giclees excluded; work on paper must be matted, framed, glazed and wired ready to hang. Each artist may enter up to five juried works, of which only one may reach 40 inches in any direction including frame. One $35 entry fee covers the juried entry and also opens the show's Small Works showcase (pieces up to 14 x 18 inches, priced at $500 or less) and its Portfolio showcase (up to ten works shown in a floor-standing print rack) at no extra charge. Six judging categories carry the awards: Animal Kingdom, Abstract/Non-Objective, Natural Environment, Figurative, Still Life/Florals and Built Environment. Show awards are $400 for Best in Show, $300 for Best of Tewksbury (a recognisable local building, site or scene) and the $200 Marion Katnack award for a Tewksbury landscape, with $125, $75 and $25 plus honourable mentions in each category. Artists are notified on 21 August, deliver work in person on 27 or 28 September, and collect unsold work on 10 October, with $25 a day charged on anything left unclaimed; the Society retains 30% commission on sales. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $400 Best in Show + category awards.

item.title: MacDowell Fellowship — Spring/Summer 2027
item.description: MacDowell's Spring/Summer 2027 cycle, for residencies running March 1 – August 31, 2027 at the 450-acre estate in Peterborough, New Hampshire. A Fellowship consists of exclusive use of a private studio, accommodations and three prepared meals a day for up to eight weeks; there are no residency fees, and Fellows may apply for need-based stipends and travel reimbursement covering direct travel, rent, lost income and childcare. Photographers apply under Visual Arts, which MacDowell describes as spanning "photographers and printmakers to sculptors and creators of large-scale installation". The sole criterion for acceptance is artistic excellence and artists at any stage of practice may apply, but applicants cannot be enrolled in a degree-seeking program during the residency season and may submit only one application every 24 months; the reference-letter requirement is temporarily suspended. Applications open August 17, 2026. A $30 processing fee applies, with waivers available on request for financial hardship. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Funded residency up to 8 weeks.

item.title: QM-Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Emerging Artists 2027–28
item.description: The eighth iteration of the Queens Museum's fellowship for emerging visual artists living in the five boroughs of New York City. Two artists each receive $20,000, professional development consultations with QM staff, and four mentorship and feedback sessions over the year with an established New York artist of their choosing. Each fellowship runs one year and culminates in a solo project exhibition at the Queens Museum in 2028; the award covers the artist fee, materials and production costs for the work made for that show. Emerging is defined as at least two but no more than ten years of practice outside a degree programme, with no solo exhibitions at established commercial galleries or museums and no major grants; age and formal training are not factors. Applications are reviewed by QM curatorial staff and two guest jurors, with in-person interviews for shortlisted candidates in November. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $20,000 × 2 + solo exhibition.

item.title: Brightwork Fellowship 2027
item.description: Anchorlight's flagship studio-based fellowship for one North Carolina artist a year at a pivotal moment in their career: a 500-plus square foot studio at Anchorlight in Raleigh, a solo exhibition in its zero-commission gallery, and an unrestricted award of $50,000. Anchorlight is home to 28 artist studios and a 1,500 square foot gallery; the Brightwork programme began in 2017 and relaunched under the current model in 2022, with the Brightwork Foundation formed in late 2025 to steward it. Applicants must have lived in North Carolina full time for at least twelve consecutive months and commit to staying for the fellowship. The same cycle also offers two Brightwork Grants to NC-based visual artists — a $2,000 Professional Development Grant and a $3,000 Studio Project Grant — but you may apply for only one of the three. Practising visual artists 21 and over of any career stage are eligible; performers, filmmakers, musicians and writers are not. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: See website. Prize: $50,000 + studio + solo exhibition.

item.title: ON::View Artist Residency — February–May 2027
item.description: A fully funded residency in a street-level storefront studio at ARTS Southeast in Savannah's Starland District, where large east-facing windows let the neighbourhood watch the work happen around the clock. The residency provides free use of the 12-by-12-foot studio, free lodging at the nearby 5th Dimension Apartment and a $500 stipend that may go to travel, materials or anything the resident chooses, for an artist or curator making new work, continuing a project or doing research. Residents are encouraged to give a public lecture, workshop or other interactive event, and must work in the studio during ARTS Southeast's public open hours at least one day a week. Open internationally and to collaborative teams; artists may work in any medium suitable for the space, and current or recent ARTS Southeast studio members are not eligible. Programme partners include the SCAD Museum of Art and Telfair Museums. The $50 application fee can be waived on request if it is an undue burden. — Deadline: September 7, 2026. Fee: $50. Prize: Funded residency + $500 stipend.
